candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed page 14, Physiological Adaptation: manage care of a client receiving hemodialysis; monitor and respond to fluid/electrolyte-related complications.
candidate.educational_objective: Use postdialysis weight relative to target dry weight as a clinical indicator of volume management and fluid removal during hemodialysis.

options.A: Assess whether excess fluid removal has brought the client toward the intended volume status
options.B: Determine dialysis solute clearance without using laboratory data
options.C: Diagnose a change in nutritional status from this single treatment

candidate.rationale: NIDDK defines dry weight as the weight after hemodialysis has removed extra fluid and explains that controlling fluid intake helps the client remain at the proper dry weight. Hemodialysis removes excess fluid by ultrafiltration. Comparing the postdialysis weight with the target weight therefore helps assess the client's volume-management result. B is incorrect because solute clearance is not established from weight alone. C overinterprets a single treatment-related weight change, which is largely driven by fluid removal. D requires assessment of the access/dialysis circuit rather than body weight.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Target/dry weight represents the intended postdialysis volume state after excess fluid removal, so postdialysis weight is used to assess volume-management progress rather than solute clearance or access flow.

candidate.stem: After a hemodialysis session, the RN compares the client's postdialysis weight with the prescribed target (dry) weight. What is the primary purpose of this comparison?
